title: Selena Gomez's Rare Beauty Just Landed in India. Good Luck Getting Your Hands on That Blush.
excerpt: The beauty brand that conquered TikTok and redefined clean-girl makeup is now on Nykaa — online and in 30 stores. The Soft Pinch Liquid Blush alone could sell out before you finish reading this.
body:
There are celebrity beauty brands. And then there is **Rare Beauty**.

When **Selena Gomez** launched her line in September 2020 — in the middle of a global pandemic, no less — skeptics dismissed it as another famous face slapping her name on a tube of lip gloss. Six years later, the Soft Pinch Liquid Blush has become one of the most viral makeup products in internet history, and Gomez herself has become a billionaire with the brand as a cornerstone of her empire.

Now, Rare Beauty has arrived in India. And the timing couldn't be sharper.

**Nykaa** — India's dominant beauty retail platform — has partnered with Rare Beauty to launch the brand across its website, mobile app, and **30 physical stores** nationwide. The debut lineup reads like a greatest-hits playlist: the legendarily pigmented **Soft Pinch Liquid Blush**, the impossibly balanced **Soft Pinch Tinted Lip Oil**, and the **True to Myself Natural Matte Longwear Foundation** — lightweight, breathable, and designed to work across skin tones without looking like a mask.

> "India's premium beauty landscape is evolving rapidly, led by a new generation of highly informed and globally engaged consumers." — Anchit Nayar, CEO, Nykaa Beauty

For the Indian diaspora, this is the end of a long suitcase game. NRIs in the US, UK, and Canada have been stocking up on Rare Beauty at Sephora for years — and then carrying extras home as gifts for cousins, friends, and that one aunt in Pune who watched a Soft Pinch Blush tutorial on Instagram and hasn't stopped asking since. That informal supply chain is now officially unnecessary.

The Indian beauty market is on a tear — projected to hit $28 billion by 2028 — and global brands have been falling over themselves to get in. But Rare Beauty's entry hits different. This isn't just another luxury label parachuting into Mumbai for the upper crust. Gomez has built something that resonates with a younger Indian consumer who grew up on her Disney Channel era, streamed *Only Murders in the Building* religiously, and follows her across Instagram — where she remains one of the most-followed women on the planet.

https://www.instagram.com/p/DZP-VyOgv9W/

What elevates Rare Beauty beyond a celebrity vanity project is its **Rare Impact Fund** — a commitment to donate one percent of all global sales to increase access to mental health services for young people, with a stated goal of raising $100 million over a decade. In a country where mental health conversations are still often whispered rather than spoken, where therapy carries stigma and resources remain uneven, that mission carries real weight. It isn't just marketing. It's baked into every purchase.

The products themselves hold up to the mythology. The **Soft Pinch Liquid Blush** is absurdly pigmented — one dot on the back of your hand blooms into a flush that lasts through humidity, commutes, and the full emotional arc of a workday. The **Tinted Lip Oil** strikes the sweet spot between moisture and color that most lip products fumble. And the **Foundation** is the kind of weightless formula that Indian humidity demands — it sits on skin without melting by noon, disappears into your texture rather than sitting on top of it, and comes in a shade range that actually accounts for South Asian skin tones.

Nykaa's hybrid retail model gives the launch an advantage that pure e-commerce plays can't match: the ability to swatch, test, and be seduced in person. With stores across Delhi, Mumbai, Bangalore, Hyderabad, and beyond, the in-store experience is built to convert the curious. Online, Nykaa's logistics mean same-day or next-day delivery in major metros — which is going to matter, because the Soft Pinch Blush in shade **Joy** has a history of disappearing from shelves faster than anyone can restock it.

The brand's vegan, cruelty-free credentials tick another box for a generation of Indian consumers who are increasingly selective about what goes on their skin and where it comes from. Rare Beauty isn't just selling makeup. It's selling a philosophy — that beauty should feel effortless, inclusive, and like an act of self-expression rather than self-correction.

For Selena Gomez, India represents one of the last major beauty markets the brand hadn't cracked. For Indian consumers — and especially for the diaspora watching from abroad — this launch is validation that the product they've been recommending for years has finally come home.

Pack the suitcase lighter next trip. The blush is already there.
